nodes.notes: Looks up an existing HubSpot contact by last-modified date — finds records the pipeline hasn't processed yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Job Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Diff the Two Systems
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Count In-Sync Rows
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Apply Updates to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Job Tracker', matched on jobId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Backfill into HubSpot
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Gather Sync Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Replicate records between tools for integrations

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers integrations work end to end across Google Sheets, HubSpot and Slack.

It moves through 14 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Pull Side A (HubSpot)
3. Pull Side B (Google Sheets)
4. Diff the Two Systems
5. Create Missing in Google Sheets
6. Count In-Sync Rows
7. Apply Updates to Google Sheets
8. Backfill into HubSpot
9. Gather Sync Results
10. Guard Non-Empty type
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Summarize Run Stats
13. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
14. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing integrations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Pull Side A (HubSpot) → Pull Side B (Google Sheets) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in Google Sheets → Count In-Sync Rows → Apply Updates to Google Sheets → Backfill into HubSpot → Gather Sync Results → Guard Non-Empty type → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and HubSpot aligned by hand for integrations
- Reconciling Google Sheets against HubSpot after the two quietly drifted apart
- Integrations work where "Pull Side A (HubSpot)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Integrations work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and HubSpot in step for integrations, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares Google Sheets against HubSpot before writing, so only genuine differences land
- A failed Google Sheets or HubSpot call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 16 nodes in this integrations build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a integrations run reports once rather than 16 times
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for integrations

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your integrations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole integrations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
